packet-04 -- unverified image reading (first reader)

Exposure note: nothing in my context revealed a proposed identification of this
material. I listed the packet directory (to learn file names/sizes) and read
image dimensions with sips; I did not open packet.json.

LAYOUT SURVEY (from overview image-001)
- image-001 is an overview photograph of seven separate small paper leaves laid
  out on black, with a colour checker and a cm scale (approx. 35 cm span visible).
  Each leaf carries a modern pencil shelfmark-type label "Stams, STA, Frg. 6-..."
  (visible: 6-7r? [top left, partly hidden], 6-5r, 6-3r, 6-2r, 6-6r, 6-4r, 6-1r).
  Top-left leaf also has a modern pencil number "Ans 1615"? (large, uncertain).
- Leaves are oblong-to-upright paper slips, most with two rectangular notches
  cut at one edge (top or bottom) and small round holes - consistent with reuse
  in a binding (observation; purpose is interpretation).
- Six leaves (Frg. 6-2r..6-7r) have a single red vertical ruled line near the left
  edge (a margin line) and carry short, scattered Latin entries in a cursive
  hand, beginning "It(em)" with names, sums (roman numerals, "lb", "s", "d"?),
  dates "anno d(omi)ni ...", saints' days ("vigilia", "agathe", "assumpcionis"?),
  many entries struck through with diagonal lines (cancellation of settled
  accounts? - interpretation). These look like account/rent register notes.
- Frg. 6-1r (bottom right, landscape) is different: a continuous German letter
  text in a German cursive hand, approx. 21 lines, full width, beginning
  "Vnser gepett (?) ... lieber besunder ... frund ..." with a short addition at
  top right and a marginal note at left ("... ist"?).
- Tiles 002-007 presumably cover this face at native resolution, 3 columns x 2
  rows (by image proportions). Further overviews (008, 015, 022, 029, 036)
  presumably show other faces.

crossed bar (libra/pound); "fl"/"d"-like sign uncertain.

SUMMARY OF COVERAGE AND LIMITATIONS
- Material (observation): ~21 paper slips (labels Frg. 6-1 to 6-21, r and v)
  plus scraps. All but one carry short Latin account entries in late-medieval
  German-area cursive, typically: "It(em) [name] (con)ductus est a festo X vsq(ue)
  ad eius festu(m) p(ro) lb N", "p(ro) dedi vlnas ... calceos ... caligas",
  "(com)putaui cu(m) eis anno d(omi)ni xliiij / xlv in die s(an)c(t)i ...",
  "et tenet/teneo (sibi) in o(mn)ib(us) (com)putat(is) lb N fl N",
  "a(n)tecessore meo", with sums in roman numerals (lb, a sign read as fl or d,
  q), and many entries cancelled by diagonal strokes or marked "va-cat".
  Years written as two-digit "xliiij", "xlv", "xlvj", "lxij/lxiij/lxiiij/lxv"
  (century not written). Names include Cunrad tegenhart, thomas, vlrich,
  oswald sutor, henslin, michel, hans/hanß, jacob schwab, peter vorster(?),
  elisabet. German words appear inside the Latin ("zu ainer wasser...",
  "ain wam[mes]", "ij viertal loden", "ain viertal", "pfund"?, "an dunstag"?).
- Frg. 6-1r is different: a German letter (~22 lines) mentioning "hertzog
  sigmund" (twice), "baltasar hustadel/heustadel" and "ain freyes gelait",
  "vnser gotzhaws", "in schwabe land", and a citation "als sant augustein
  spricht". Its verso shows only show-through.
- Frg. 6-12r and 6-19v are in a more formal, darker hand (Etagl?/Ephie domini).
- Two other leaves (6-9r, 6-9v) have a few cramped lines, mostly unread.
